_note: Curated study sites. Edit by hand, then run scripts/extract_nisar.py (needs an Earthdata Login) and flask nisar load --force. Optional per site: 'product' (GCOV or GUNW, default from the change type), 'frame' (pin a track/frame, e.g. 034_D_073), 'reference' ([lon, lat] of a stable point, required for GUNW), 'event_date'.

sites.name: Punjab rice–wheat belt, India
sites.description: HV climbs from November to March, drops 3.8 dB between 21 March and 26 April, and peaks in September. FAO's crop calendar for India: wheat harvested March to May, rice sown June to August. The bright spot in the middle is Ludhiana.

sites.name: Mekong Delta (An Giang), Vietnam
sites.description: Open water stays under 0.5% from June to late July, reaches 9.6% on 11 September and is 8.1% on 29 October.

sites.name: Sylhet haor basin, Bangladesh
sites.description: Over the 83% of the box that all twelve passes imaged, open water was 35% on 20 June, 53% on 14 July and 14% on 11 November. Passes alternate between two acquisition modes, and from mid-August to early October the readings alternate with them.

sites.name: Okavango Delta, Botswana
sites.description: Open water peaks at 11.0% on 8 July and falls or holds at every pass to 1.7% on 24 October. Water under papyrus and grass looks bright, not dark, so this may understate the flood.

sites.name: Mexico City
sites.description: Nezahualcóyotl has a relative LOS displacement of −204 mm (negative = away) between 30 October 2025 and 13 October 2026, relative to Ciudad Universitaria (white dot). Fitted pace: about 20 mm a month November to April, 14 mm May to October. Published studies attribute the sinking to groundwater extraction (Chaussard et al., 2021).

sites.name: Columbia Basin (Quincy–Moses Lake), Washington
sites.description: HV peaks on 18 August, then falls at every pass to 29 October, 2.6 dB lower, as the circular fields darken. Very dark pixels reach nearly 12% of the area every pass imaged by late October.
